target.spec_url_note: stable alias; spec version recorded as 12.1.0
target.client_url_note: version-pinned path; the latest-stable alias used during collection is mutable and should not be cited
target.client_archive_note: The server re-compresses this archive, so its SHA-256 is not stable: two fetches of the same pinned URL gave 56c1c79a... and ae7f2d57.... Verify the extracted client by content digest instead.
target.client_content_note: sha256 over the 986 extracted .js files, each contributing its repo-relative posix path then the sha256 of its bytes, ordered by path. 26,274,040 bytes total. Stable across re-compression.

results.row_vs_path_note: 24 extracted rows map to 23 distinct normalised paths because /Users and /Users/ both appear; precision is computed over rows, recall over distinct paths

note: Precision against a published specification is a lower bound: a route absent from the spec is not necessarily absent from the server. The router-path class was identified post hoc from the misses.

repaired_classifier.recall_note: equals the extraction ceiling already reported for the original run; not a classification gain

absolute_third_party_rows.note: the cost of the relaxed default

repaired_classifier.noise_sensitivity: excluding strings containing template syntax, whitespace, markup characters or a static-asset extension before measuring changes precision by less than one point on both Jellyfin runs

criterion.primary: repaired recall reaches >= 90% of the measured extraction ceiling
criterion.note: A ceiling-relative primary is the correct form: an absolute point-gain requirement would be imposed on a quantity bounded by a ceiling that differs per application.

zulip.verdict: partially generalized - secondary missed by 13.3 points

immich.scope_condition: @immich/sdk is code-generated from the specification used as ground truth, so its precision measures the generator, not the classifier. Valid test of ceiling and tier; invalid test of precision.

three_application_evaluation.generalized: repaired recall equals 100% of the extraction ceiling on all three applications
did_not_generalize: evidence tier - spread +40.1 on Jellyfin and +9.2 on Zulip against a +20 bar; not assessable on Immich
three_application_evaluation.extraction_ceiling_mechanism: neither relative-path pattern spans a template interpolation whose contents are non-trivial; the plain-path character class excludes parentheses and the template pattern tolerates one interpolation under 60 chars with no closing brace. Jellyfin carries literal {itemId} braces and is unaffected.
three_application_evaluation.proposed_fix: interpolation-aware scanner; PROPOSED AND NOT APPLIED. Recorded prediction: Immich ceiling 82.8% -> ~99%, Jellyfin essentially unchanged.

tier.definition: request-construction precision minus absent-evidence precision, assigned by classifier_rule.classify_endpoint over every relative-path record in the extraction
tier.bar: +20 points for the tier to be said to carry signal

immich.not_assessable_because: the artefact yields one false positive among 167 relative rows (the base path /api), against 177 of 424 on Jellyfin, so no tier has anything to discriminate and the spread is zero by construction

tier.conclusion: strong signal on one of the two assessable applications and none on the other; not a general operating point without per-application calibration
